findings.title: T-01 spoofing: forged/guessed/revoked API key accepted
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-01 (SAD.md §6, boundary TB-01): a caller forges or guesses an API key, or uses a revoked key, to act as another principal.
findings.code_snippet:
digest = hash_key(presented)
api_key = uow.api_keys.get_by_hash(digest)
if api_key is None or not _is_active(api_key, digest):
    raise Unauthenticated("invalid API key")
...
return hmac.compare_digest(api_key.key_hash, digest) and api_key.revoked_at is None
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: SHA-256 hashed keys compared with hmac.compare_digest; revoked_at rejects; missing/invalid key returns 401. Attempted exploit vs the code: a forged/guessed plaintext hashes to a digest that misses the index -> get_by_hash None -> 401 (L69). A revoked key matches the hash but _is_active returns False because revoked_at is not None (L87) -> 401. Missing key -> Unauthenticated at L65-66. Keys carry 256 bits of entropy (KEY_ENTROPY_BYTES=32, L24). compare_digest is constant-time. The attack is blocked.
findings.attack_vector: T-01 spoofing / TB-01: forged, guessed, or revoked X-API-Key header presented to a /v1 route.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit a random/forged key, and separately a key whose revoked_at is set, to an authenticated endpoint.

resolution.refute_evidence: auth.verify L65-71 rejects missing/unmatched keys with 401; _is_active L87 rejects revoked keys via `revoked_at is None`; compare_digest is constant-time. Proven by passing test_sec_t01 (test_fr03.py:302).

findings.title: T-02 elevation_of_privilege: lower-scope key reaches higher-scope endpoint
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-02 (TB-01): a read or write key calls an endpoint requiring a higher scope.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: single scope dependency applied to every /v1 route, evaluated before resource lookup. Verified every /v1 route declares guard() with the correct scope: routes_tasks (write/read/read/admin), routes_runs (write/read), routes_metrics (admin) — grep confirms no /v1 route omits guard. FastAPI runs route dependencies before the handler body, so require_scope.check (L87-89) raises 403 before any lookup. scope_includes uses the ordered SCOPES index (auth.py L74-79), so read(0)<write(1)<admin(2). The attack is blocked.
findings.verify_evidence: test_sec_t02_insufficient_scope_returns_403 (03-development/tests/test_fr04.py:184) passes; every /v1 route uses guard() (routes_tasks.py L31/45/55/72, routes_runs.py L36/49, routes_metrics.py L21).
findings.attack_vector: T-02 EoP / TB-01: authenticate with a read/write key, call an endpoint whose guard requires a higher scope.
findings.attempted_exploit: Call DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} (guard admin) and POST /v1/tasks (guard write) with a read-scope key.

resolution.refute_evidence: guard() (deps.py L94-99) is declared on every /v1 route with the correct scope; require_scope.check (L87-89) runs as a dependency before the handler and raises Forbidden. Proven by passing test_sec_t02 (test_fr04.py:184).

findings.title: T-03 information_disclosure: 403 vs 404 reveals task existence
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-03 (TB-01): 403 versus 404 responses reveal whether a task id exists to a caller lacking scope.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: authorization decided before lookup; 403 body identical regardless of resource existence. require_scope runs as a dependency before the handler (so an under-scoped caller always gets 403 whether or not the id exists), and the 403 problem body omits `instance` (error_handlers L47) so the path cannot differentiate. A caller lacking scope therefore cannot distinguish a real from a missing id. The attack is blocked.
findings.attack_vector: T-03 info disclosure / TB-01: probe task ids with an under-scoped key and compare 403 vs 404.
findings.attempted_exploit: Request a known-missing and a known-existing task id with insufficient scope; compare status and body.

resolution.refute_evidence: Scope check precedes lookup (deps.py L87-89 dependency order); 403 body sets instance=None (error_handlers.py L47). Proven by passing test_sec_t03 (test_fr04.py:196).

findings.title: T-04 denial_of_service: token flood exhausts workers/pool
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-04 (TB-01): a token floods the API to exhaust workers or the connection pool.
findings.code_snippet:
bucket = uow.rate_buckets.get_for_update(key_id)
tokens = _refilled_tokens(bucket, capacity=capacity, rate_per_sec=rate_per_sec, now=now)
allowed = tokens >= _TOKEN_COST
if allowed:
    tokens -= _TOKEN_COST
uow.rate_buckets.save(bucket, key_id, tokens, now)
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: per-token DB-backed token bucket under row lock; 429 with Retry-After; bounded concurrency and pool. consume() reads the bucket FOR UPDATE (SQLite serialized via BEGIN IMMEDIATE, session.py L75-90), refills capped at capacity (_refilled_tokens L78-88), and denies when tokens < 1 returning a Retry-After of at least 1s (_seconds_until_token L91-96). deps.rate_limit raises RateLimited (429) on denial. Concurrency is bounded by the executor cap and the DB pool_size. The flood is throttled.
findings.verify_evidence: test_sec_t04_burst_exceeded_returns_429 (03-development/tests/test_fr05.py:205) passes; ratelimit.py L57-96, session.py L75-90.
findings.attack_vector: T-04 DoS / TB-01: single token issues a burst beyond capacity.
findings.attempted_exploit: Fire capacity+1 requests with one key within a refill window; expect a 429 with Retry-After.

resolution.refute_evidence: Row-locked token bucket (ratelimit.consume L57-75 over BEGIN IMMEDIATE, session.py L88-90) denies with 429+Retry-After (deps.rate_limit L72-74). Proven by passing test_sec_t04 (test_fr05.py:205).

findings.title: T-05 tampering: injection-laden task payload persisted/executed
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-05 (TB-01): malformed or injection-laden task payload is persisted or later executed.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: pydantic validation, length cap, injection-character blacklist, uniqueness check; 422 on violation. validate_command rejects empty, >1000 chars, and any of ;&|`$<>\n\r (L25,37) with ValidationFailed->422. validate_name caps length to the column width (L48-49) so a Conflict/length is a 422 not a DB error. Uniqueness enforced by the repository on insert (repository/tasks.py L75-78 -> 409). Combined with T-06 (exec, never shell), a persisted payload cannot inject a shell. The attack is blocked at validation.
findings.attack_vector: T-05 tampering / TB-01: create a task whose command contains shell metacharacters.
findings.attempted_exploit: POST a task with command containing ';', '|', '`', '$', newline; expect 422.

resolution.refute_evidence: validate_command (service/tasks.py L28-38) rejects the blacklist and length; execution uses exec not shell (T-06). Proven by passing test_sec_t05 (test_fr01.py:400).

findings.title: T-06 elevation_of_privilege: task command interpreted by a shell
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-06 (TB-02): task command is interpreted by a shell, allowing command chaining beyond the intended program.
findings.code_snippet:
argv = shlex.split(command)
if not argv:
    raise ValueError("empty command")
process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    *argv,
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
)
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: shlex.split into create_subprocess_exec; shell=True forbidden and grep-gated. run_command tokenizes with shlex.split (L120) and spawns via create_subprocess_exec(*argv) (L123) which passes argv directly to execve with no shell. Shell metacharacters become literal argv tokens, not operators; chaining (`;`, `|`, `$()`) cannot execute a second program. No create_subprocess_shell / shell=True anywhere. The attack is blocked.
findings.attack_vector: T-06 EoP / TB-02: a task command crafted to chain commands if a shell interprets it.
findings.attempted_exploit: Run a command containing ';'/'|'/'$()' and verify the second program never executes.

resolution.refute_evidence: runner.run_command uses shlex.split + create_subprocess_exec(*argv) (L120-127); no shell is invoked. Proven by passing test_sec_t06 (test_fr02.py:388). (Validation layer T-05 also blocks these chars before execution.)

findings.title: T-07 denial_of_service: hung task leaves orphan process/held resources
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-07 (TB-02): a long-running or hung task leaves an orphan process and holds resources.
findings.code_snippet:
async def _kill(process):
    process.kill()
    await process.wait()
...
stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(process.communicate(), timeout)
...
except TimeoutError:
    await _kill(process)
    stdout, stderr, status = b"", b"", TIMEOUT
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    await _kill(process)
    raise
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: asyncio.wait_for timeout; process.kill() then await process.wait(); drain timeout marks interrupted. run_command bounds execution with wait_for (L132); on TimeoutError and on CancelledError it calls _kill which kill()s then await wait()s (L93-99), reaping the child so no orphan is left; CancelledError is re-raised (L139). executor.drain (L91-109) waits up to DRAIN_TIMEOUT then cancels in-flight tasks and awaits them so their kill+reap runs, and drops queued jobs via on_dropped (-> interrupted). The resource leak is blocked.
findings.attack_vector: T-07 DoS / TB-02: submit a task that hangs past the timeout.
findings.attempted_exploit: Run a sleep-forever command; assert it is killed+reaped at TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT with no surviving PID.

resolution.refute_evidence: wait_for timeout (runner.py L132) then _kill = kill()+await wait() (L93-99) reaps the child; drain cancels+awaits in-flight (executor.py L100-108). Proven by passing test_sec_t07 (test_fr08.py:401).

findings.title: T-08 tampering: SQL injection via string-built queries
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-08 (TB-03): SQL injection through string-built queries alters or reads other rows.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: ORM or parameterized statements only; no f-string or concatenated SQL; grep gate. All reads/writes use SQLAlchemy constructs (select/where/and_/or_/delete, L102-124); status and cursor values flow in as bound parameters via column comparisons (Task.status == status, after_cursor decodes to datetime/str params L48-57). No f-string or `+`-built SQL. decode_cursor validates input and raises ValidationFailed on malformed data (L36-45). Metacharacters are treated as data. The injection is blocked.
findings.attack_vector: T-08 tampering / TB-03: inject SQL via status filter or cursor.
findings.attempted_exploit: List tasks with a status like "' OR 1=1 --"; expect it matched literally, no extra rows.

resolution.refute_evidence: Queries are SQLAlchemy ORM with bound parameters only (repository/tasks.py L102-124); cursor decoded+validated (L36-45). Proven by passing test_sec_t08 (test_fr01.py:411).

findings.title: T-09 tampering: v3 migration loses/corrupts result data on up/downgrade
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-09 (TB-03): v3 data migration loses or corrupts result data on upgrade or downgrade.
findings.code_snippet:
op.execute(_SPLIT_RESULTS)
op.drop_column("tasks", "result_json")
...
op.add_column("tasks", sa.Column("result_json", sa.Text()))
op.execute(_FOLD_RESULTS)
op.drop_index(...)
op.drop_table("task_results")
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: reversible real downgrade; round-trip test comparing every column on a real SQLite file. Upgrade splits tasks.result_json (array, or single object normalized via json_array(json(...)), L41-42) into task_results rows preserving exit_code/stdout_tail/stderr_tail/duration_ms/finished_at and the id (COALESCE to a random id when absent, L37). Downgrade folds them back with json_group_array/json_object (L46-53) keeping each column and type. Both use literal SQL so offline render works. The round-trip test asserts every column survives. Data is preserved for the declared v3<->v2 round trip; the only non-exact case (a v1 single-object result_json becomes a one-element array) is intentional normalization documented at L2-6.
findings.suggested_fix: None required for the declared round trip; mitigation effective.
findings.verify_evidence: test_sec_t09_v3_roundtrip_preserves_data (03-development/tests/test_fr07.py:378) passes on a real SQLite file; v3_split_results.py L35-80.
findings.attack_vector: T-09 tampering / TB-03: upgrade/downgrade the v3 migration and check for data loss/corruption.
findings.attempted_exploit: Round-trip a DB with populated task_results through downgrade then upgrade and compare every column.

resolution.refute_evidence: Real reversible up/downgrade (v3_split_results.py L56-80) preserving all result columns and types via json_extract/json_group_array. Proven by passing round-trip test_sec_t09 (test_fr07.py:378).

findings.title: T-10 repudiation: failed request not traceable to actor/cause
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-10 (TB-03): a failed request cannot be traced to its actor or cause across client and server.
findings.code_snippet:
correlation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
scope.setdefault("state", {})["correlation_id"] = correlation_id
...
MutableHeaders(scope=message)[CORRELATION_HEADER] = correlation_id
...
logger.exception("unhandled error", extra={"correlation_id": correlation_id})
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: correlation_id in X-Correlation-Id header, problem body and server log. Middleware mints a uuid per request, stores it on scope state (L48-49), echoes it in the X-Correlation-Id response header via send_with_header (L56), and logs unhandled errors with it (L62-63). error_handlers.problem_response reads request.state.correlation_id and both logs the problem with it (L39-41) and includes it in every problem body (L48). The same id ties client header, body and server log. Traceability holds.
findings.attack_vector: T-10 repudiation / TB-03: a failing request with no shared id across tiers.
findings.attempted_exploit: Trigger an error and assert the same correlation id appears in the response header, body and the server log.

resolution.refute_evidence: correlation id minted per request and surfaced in header (middleware.py L56), body and log (error_handlers.py L40,L48). Proven by passing test_sec_t10 (test_fr10.py:423).

findings.title: T-11 information_disclosure: secrets leak via output tails/logs/metrics
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-11 (TB-04): secrets (sk- keys, tokens, Bearer values, DB URL with password) leak via stored output tails, logs or metrics.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: single redaction pass replaces matching lines with [REDACTED]; DB URL excluded from repr, logs and metrics. redact() replaces every line containing an sk- key, token=, Bearer, or postgres(ql):// URL with [REDACTED] (keeping the newline), and runner.tail applies it before truncation (runner.py L83-90) so a cut-off secret cannot escape. Settings.db_url is field(repr=False) (config.py L27) so it is absent from repr/logs; health.metrics (health.py L73-83) returns only counts/percentiles/rejections, never the DB URL. For every secret class named in the declared threat the leak is blocked.
findings.suggested_fix: Mitigation effective for declared secret classes. See redact#tq-gap for an out-of-scope observation about this system's own tq_ keys.
findings.verify_evidence: test_sec_t11_secrets_redacted_in_output_and_logs (03-development/tests/test_fr02.py:405) passes; redact.py L13-24, runner.py L83-90, config.py L27, health.py L73-83.
findings.attack_vector: T-11 info disclosure / TB-04: a task prints sk-/token=/Bearer/postgres URL secrets that get stored or logged.
findings.attempted_exploit: Run a command echoing each declared secret shape; assert output tails and logs show [REDACTED], and metrics/repr never contain the DB URL.

resolution.refute_evidence: redact() (redact.py L16-24) redacts each declared secret class line-wise before truncation (runner.py L90); db_url repr-excluded (config.py L27) and absent from metrics (health.py L79-83). Proven by passing test_sec_t11 (test_fr02.py:405).

findings.title: T-12 information_disclosure: error bodies expose stack traces/SQL/paths
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-12 (TB-04): 500 or other error bodies expose stack traces, SQL or file paths.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: whitelisted generic detail text; unexpected exceptions logged server-side only. An unhandled Exception is caught by CorrelationMiddleware (middleware.py L61-68) and rendered as InternalError whose detail is the fixed GENERIC_DETAIL 'An internal error occurred.' (errors.py L58-62) -- the original exception text (SQL, paths, traceback) never reaches the body, only logger.exception server-side (middleware.py L62). Request-validation failures return a generic 'request is invalid' (L74) instead of pydantic internals. Domain errors carry only their own whitelisted detail. No internal detail leaks.
findings.verify_evidence: test_sec_t12_500_body_has_no_internal_details (03-development/tests/test_fr10.py:442) passes; errors.py L50-62, middleware.py L61-68, error_handlers.py L66-74.
findings.attack_vector: T-12 info disclosure / TB-04: force a 500/validation error and inspect the body for internals.
findings.attempted_exploit: Trigger an unhandled exception and a validation error; assert the body carries only generic text and no SQL/path/traceback.

resolution.refute_evidence: Unhandled exceptions become InternalError.GENERIC_DETAIL (errors.py L58-62) via middleware (L61-68), logged server-side only; validation detail is generic (error_handlers.py L74). Proven by passing test_sec_t12 (test_fr10.py:442).

findings.title: T-13 spoofing: cross-origin page drives the API via a victim browser
findings.description: Declared STRIDE threat T-13 (TB-01): cross-origin web page drives the API using a victim's browser.
findings.reasoning: Declared mitigation: CORS allows no origin unless listed in TASKQ_CORS_ORIGINS. config.load_settings parses TASKQ_CORS_ORIGINS into a tuple, defaulting to empty (config.py L59-63). app wires Starlette CORSMiddleware with allow_origins=list(cors_origins) (app.py L110); with an empty list no origin is allowed (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is emitted for any Origin), so a browser blocks cross-origin reads. Authentication still requires X-API-Key, which a cross-origin page cannot read. The attack is blocked by default.
findings.attack_vector: T-13 spoofing / TB-01: a cross-origin site issues credentialed requests expecting CORS to permit the response.
findings.attempted_exploit: Send a request with an Origin header and default (empty) TASKQ_CORS_ORIGINS; assert no permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin is returned.

resolution.refute_evidence: CORSMiddleware is configured with allow_origins = the (empty-by-default) TASKQ_CORS_ORIGINS list (app.py L110, config.py L59-63), denying all origins. Proven by passing test_sec_t13 (test_fr10.py:461).

findings.title: redact pattern does not cover this system's own tq_ API keys
findings.description: SECRET_PATTERN matches sk- keys, token=, Bearer and postgres URLs, but this system issues keys with the tq_ prefix (auth.KEY_PREFIX, auth.py L23). A task whose stdout/stderr contains a tq_ key is stored and returned via run history without redaction.
findings.reasoning: Observation beyond the declared T-11 threat scope (T-11 enumerates sk-/token/Bearer/DB-URL only, all of which ARE covered). Practical exploitability is low: to leak a key it must appear in a task's own captured output, and the authenticated caller who supplies the command already holds a key; there is no realistic path by which another principal's tq_ key enters a victim command's output. Recorded for tracking, not a declared-threat violation.
findings.suggested_fix: If tq_ keys are considered output-sensitive, add `tq_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}` to SECRET_PATTERN.
findings.verify_evidence: redact.py L13 pattern lists no tq_ alternative; auth.py L23 KEY_PREFIX='tq_'.
